title: Snapshot Isolation Read with Unchecked Clock Uncertainty
pattern: Reading or committing versioned snapshot data in a clock-coordinated distributed database (such as Spanner or CockroachDB equivalents) at the current local system timestamp without factoring in or waiting out the clock's confidence interval or uncertainty bound (\(\epsilon\)).
why_bad: In clock-synchronized distributed systems, every clock reading has a confidence interval \([earliest, latest]\) representing the physical clock uncertainty [152, 154]. If two transactions occur within the uncertainty interval of each other (overlapping confidence intervals), their relative order is ambiguous [154, 155]. Reading immediately without waiting out \(\epsilon\) violates transaction causality and external consistency (linearizability), potentially serving stale reads or missing committed writes [66, 154].
detection: Identify invocations of database reads or writes utilizing physical timestamps as snapshot boundaries, where the code does not enforce a sleep/wait duration equal to or greater than the clock uncertainty bound (e.g., TrueTime's `limit = latest - earliest`), or does not use explicit transaction coordinates.
fix: Enforce an artificial slowdown/wait time equal to the clock uncertainty interval (the TrueTime wait strategy) before committing or reading, or utilize consensus-driven logical epoch systems to eliminate physical clock dependencies [66, 92, 155].
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 8 / passages [152, 154, 155]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 13 / passage [66].
